title: Can thirty six dots be a triangle and a square?
description: Thirty six dots are stacked in eight rows to make a triangle, and laid in six rows of six to make a square. The video checks both by counting.
teaching_notes: One idea: the same number of dots can be arranged in two different shapes. Watch for students who stop at one picture and do not count to check.

source: Figure it Out Q3 (Math Talk), p.5
video_script.why: The child arranges the same thirty six dots as a triangle and as a square, the way ten dots were arranged as a triangle and a rectangle.
video_script.substitution: A number that is triangular and square can be drawn both ways with the same dots.
video_script.anchor: thirty six dots in a loose pile, with an empty triangle outline and an empty square outline beside them
video_script.payoff_line: Thirty six dots make a triangle and a square

final_answer.value: 36 dots as a triangle with 8 rows (1+2+...+8) and as a 6 by 6 square.
final_answer.spoken: thirty six dots make a triangle and a square

hold_back: 36 dots make a triangle and a square
never_show: a number can be drawn in only one way
video_script.design: One idea: the same dots make a triangle and a square. Callback to ten dots as a triangle and a rectangle. Wrong idea: none is broken. The two outlines stay on the board to the end.
